significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish a form-(iii) ordering—after controlling for billing co-occurrence, "mechanistically linked diseases are closer than diseases that merely co-occur"—together with a form-(ii) causal claim that steering a "disease-mechanism direction" selectively changes predicted risks for downstream conditions. This would fix expectations for unseen mechanism-versus-co-occurrence disease pairs and would establish a behavioral regularity plus mechanism-aligned internal geometry, although the steering result concerns prediction behavior rather than proving that the model executes the corresponding biological mechanism; this distinction matters for predictive EHR representation systems such as Med-BERT (Rasmy et al., 2021) and BEHRT (Li et al., 2020). The branches are determinate: failure of the controlled ordering and selective steering would reject this account for the examined representations, though it would not show that no other layer or representation encodes pathophysiology. Under topic substitution, generic ontology alignment would merit only the topic median, but the quoted mechanism/co-occurrence dissociation and downstream-risk coupling add a specific, constraining conclusion beyond that baseline.

reach.justification: The transferable handles are explicitly the "mechanism-alignment score" as a diagnostic and the "disease-mechanism direction" as an intervention; the former is mainly a post-hoc assessment of learned geometry, while it could also be used to audit a trained model before clinical deployment, and the latter changes risk predictions rather than forecasting a naturally occurring failure in advance. Re-extraction would be required on each model, but the conclusion predicts a transferable relation—mechanism-linked/low-co-occurrence pairs should be closer than high-co-occurrence/low-mechanism pairs—rather than merely supplying an open-ended search procedure. The hypothesis ranges over "clinical LLMs and EHR foundation models," and its plausible downstream users include model auditors and clinical-risk system developers, but it does not assert transfer beyond clinical models or provide a validated gating rule for individual patient predictions. The topic-substitution check lowers the generic scientific-representation rationale to the median, while the named audit score, intervention, and cross-model conditional ordering support reach above it.
